scope: IMP-02 / R2 item 325 follow-up: evaluate whether composer and bun have reliable installation-shape evidence, and lock the decision not to guess
question: Can composer and bun be classified into UpdateChannel by filesystem evidence, the way Corepack shims and pip-installed uv already are?

findings.candidateEvidence: A composer.bat whose body references composer.phar
findings.whyRejected: The launcher proves only that this copy wraps composer.phar. It does not prove which installer created it, so the same file shape occurs for the standalone installer, a manual phar download, and a package-manager install. Treating it as a distinct channel would mean inventing a rule with no negative case.

findings.candidateEvidence: Install path shape, or a sibling shim directory
findings.whyRejected: Every Windows bun distribution writes the same static bun.exe; scoop and winget add their own shim outside the install directory and leave no marker next to the binary. Nothing beside the resolved command distinguishes them, and a false positive would disable an update that actually works.

principle: This checker refuses only on a positive, verifiable signal. Absence of evidence is not evidence of a different installer, so an unknown shape stays Standalone instead of being guessed at.
implementation: A comment at the catch-all arm records why these two tools have no shape check, so the omission is deliberate and documented rather than an oversight.

fixtures.name: pkgtools::tests::composer_and_bun_stay_standalone_because_no_reliable_evidence_exists
asserts: a composer.bat wrapping composer.phar still reports Standalone with no blocker and yields `self-update`
a bun.exe with interpreter-looking files beside it still reports Standalone with no blocker and yields `upgrade`
the second case deliberately places python.exe and pip.exe next to bun.exe to prove the uv rule does not leak into bun

notVerified: No real composer or bun installation was inspected on this host; the decision rests on the installers' documented behaviour, not on observed files
No UI change: both tools keep the existing 'conditionally supported' wording
limitations: If a future bun or composer installer starts writing a marker next to the binary, this evaluation must be revisited
The Corepack heuristic still cannot see a shim that invokes corepack through another wrapper
IMP-02 item 325 remains unchecked: two of ten managers still lack runtime shape diagnosis, by decision rather than by omission
